texts.preamble: Narendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 20 March, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:50334 Court No. - 74 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 565 of 2009 Revisionist :- Narendra Kumar Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Santosh Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1.
texts.facts: The facts of the case are that on 30.12.1998 at about 01.00 pm the revisionist was found selling and demonstrating pulses along with other articles in his shop situated at Erwa Katra by the complainant N.R. Pandey, Food Inspector. On suspicion of it being adulterated, he disclosed his identity to the accused and purchased 750 gm gram pulse (chana daal) for sample from the accused by giving Rs.15/- and gave notice and took signature of the accused on it. After preparation of sample in three polythene bag in equal part sent to the public analyst for analysis. The public analyst found the sample to be adulterated as 1.10 per cent khesari daal was found in it. The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused. In the trial court the complainant/Ram N.R. Pandey was examined as P.W.-1, Kush Kumar Gupta, the clerk was examined as P.W.-2. The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication. No defense evidence was led. The appeal was preferred against the same which came to be dismissed after which the present revision has been filed against both the impugned judgement and orders.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that there has been inordinate delay in filing of the complaint inasmuch as the sample of the alleged food article was taken on 30.12.1998 which was sent for testing to the public analyst after which the public analyst gave its report dated 18.1.1999 but the present complaint of the case has been filed on 09.3.2000. It is submitted that subsequently notice was sent by P.W.-2 along with public analyst report through registered post as alleged on 01.4.2000. It is submitted that there has been inordinate delay of about 01 year and 02 months in filing of the complaint. It is submitted that the delay in filing of the complaint is not explained at all and is enormous. It is submitted that sending of the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with the report of public analyst to the revisionist was after about 22 days of the filing of the complaint. It is submitted that looking to the facts that the complaint has been filed after about 01 year and 2 months of the date of report of public analyst for which there is no plausible explanation given and then the said report being sent to the revisionist with notice under Section 13(2) of the Act even 22 days thereafter, clearly deprives the revisionist of exercising his valuable right under Section 13(2) of the Act. It is submitted that looking to the same, the revision be allowed and the judgement and order of the trial court along with the judgement and order of the appellate court be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the revision and submitted that there is no illegality, irregularity or infirmity in the impugned judgements and orders of the trial court court as well as the appellate court.
